trajectory.text: I’ll make the required one-action tutorial call, then check the character and start combat. I’ll use the 15-second score check to compare approaches as I go.
Combat is working. I’ve started with the bronze sword; I’ll measure that baseline, then improve damage and target choice for the peak 15-second window.
The first 20-second combat run gained 975 raw Hitpoints XP, and the measured peak is 10 real-game XP/min. Strength rose to 20. I’m moving to cows so the bot can spend less time between targets.
Cows have raised Strength to 52 and Hitpoints to 35. I’m switching toward stronger targets now; their larger health pools should keep the character attacking longer between kills.
The Al Kharid gate required a 10-coin toll and a dialogue choice. I’ve crossed it and found nine nearby warriors with 19 HP each. I’ll test them while raising Attack for better accuracy.

Warriors produced a 105 real-game XP/min peak, but the character died after food ran out. The bronze sword was retained. I’m checking a nearby giant spider area for targets with more HP and lower damage.
The nearby giant spiders are only level 2, so they won’t help much. I’m testing the route to rock crabs; their 50 HP could support a much better uninterrupted combat window if the area is reachable.

The Rellekka rock crab gate is quest restricted, and the nearby “Tree” NPCs have no Attack option. I’m moving to an accessible moss giant spawn with 60 HP and will measure whether it improves the peak.

The Rimmington moss giant coordinate is separated from this route by an impassable area. I’m returning to Al Kharid to fund a mithril scimitar through pickpocketing, then I’ll retest warriors with the stronger weapon.

Pickpocketing brought in 614 coins, but stuns lowered HP. The kebab seller works through dialogue and charges 1 coin per kebab. I’m stocking food, earning the remaining coins, and buying the mithril scimitar.
The mithril scimitar is equipped, with 13 kebabs in inventory. I’m testing a sustained warrior run now and will compare its best 15-second window with the bronze sword peak of 105 XP/min.
The scimitar raised the peak to 131 XP/min, and Strength is now 72. I’m testing a 50 HP Fremennik citizen next; its listed defence is low, which may keep damage flowing with fewer target changes.
I’ll start with the required single action, then check the character’s state and get a Defence XP baseline.
The Defence style is active, and the first hit awarded Defence XP. I’m moving to a denser combat area and will compare the measured peak rate as I change targets and equipment.
The cow field produced a peak of 86 real game XP/min. The main limit now is damage per hit: Attack and Strength are both level 10, so I’m raising those briefly before returning to Defence.
Raising Attack and Strength roughly doubled the best Defence rate to 156 XP/min. I’m testing Al Kharid warriors next; their higher health should reduce time spent switching targets.
The route to Al Kharid stopped at a toll gate. I’m getting the small coin payment through in game actions, then I’ll resume the warrior test.

The warrior test reached 288 XP/min, with health still manageable. I’m using a short background run to raise Strength while collecting nearby coin drops, then I’ll return to Defence and measure the gain.
Strength is now 65, and the background run has returned to Defence. I’m watching health closely; the next change is to secure food before testing longer combat runs.
Pickpocketing a nearby man raised cash from 46 to 181 coins in about a minute. I’m buying food, then I’ll earn enough for a stronger scimitar from Zeke.
The steel scimitar is equipped on its Defence style. I’m returning to the warrior cluster for a measured run, then I’ll decide whether more Strength or a tougher target is likely to improve the peak.
The steel run exposed a style mismatch: combat was on the shared XP style, which split damage XP across three skills. I’m correcting it to pure Defence before judging the weapon’s rate.
The remaining cash plus sale value of spare starter items appears sufficient for a mithril scimitar. I’m trading those items at Zeke, then I’ll verify its Defence style and test it.
Mithril scimitar is equipped, with pure Defence selected. I’m testing a fixed warrior room now to avoid the door and pathing stalls seen in the previous run.

The mithril run in the west palace room gained 63,800 raw Defence XP in 50 seconds, but the measured peak is still 390 XP/min. I’m raising Strength for a short stretch, then I’ll spend the remaining time on Defence in that room.
The Strength run is still active in the west room. I’ll switch back as soon as the target level is reached and use the remaining sampling windows for Defence.
The new peak is 394 XP/min. I’m keeping the mithril scimitar on pure Defence in the west room for the remaining windows, with a health retreat built into the run.
The sustained Defence run is working, with Defence now in the mid 80s. The measured peak is still 394 XP/min; I’m letting the remaining windows run while monitoring health and the score.
The peak has risen to 442 XP/min in the 29:00–29:15 sample. The bot is still training Defence through the final samples.

Completed the 30-minute Defence run. **Peak score: 442 real-game XP/min**, from 22,100 raw XP in the best 15-second sample.

The character finished at **Defence level 89**. The best setup was a mithril scimitar on the pure Defensive style against Al Kharid warriors in the west palace room.
I’ll start with the single tutorial action you specified, then get a working Fletching baseline and use the live XP samples to guide the next training method.
The tree action works. I’m checking the API and nearby ways to obtain a knife, then I’ll turn logs into the fastest available product and measure the result.
The first shaft batch gave Fletching XP. I’m leveling through normal logs now; after level 20 I’ll switch to higher tier logs, which should produce much stronger 15 second windows.
The level-up loop is still running. I’m letting that batch finish, then I’ll inspect the resulting level and current score before changing methods.
Fletching is 35 and Woodcutting is 46. Oak longbows gave 625 raw XP each; I’m moving to willow now and will compare its per log XP and throughput.
Willow shortbows are giving 832 raw XP per log. The current batch is working toward willow longbows and level 50, where I can test the next tier.

A 22 log willow batch raised the peak to 166 real game XP/min. I’m putting the repeatable gather and fletch cycle into a background script so it can keep training while I watch the sampled rate and adjust the route.

The background cycle is stable. It has reached Fletching 60, and the sampled peak is now 311 XP/min. I’m letting it reach yew bows, then I’ll decide whether another source or faster action sequence can improve the peak.
Yew shortbows have pushed the peak to 415 XP/min. The yew tree yields a useful batch before it falls; I’m tracking how quickly it respawns while working toward level 80 for magic bows.

The nearby yew is now spending more time as a stump than producing logs. Willow gave a much steadier supply, so I’m switching back to it for the remaining levels to 80, then I’ll look for magic trees.

The willow route recovered quickly and has reached Fletching 77 and Woodcutting 86. I’m keeping the batch running to level 80, then I’ll use the known Sorcerer’s Tower area to locate magic trees in game.
Fletching is now 80, Woodcutting 89, and the peak is 527 XP/min. I’m heading to the magic trees south of Sorcerer’s Tower for a higher XP per log test.

The direct route crossed White Wolf Mountain and the bot died to wolves, then respawned with the axe and knife. With the remaining time, I’m using the safe Lumbridge yew to build a concentrated yew longbow batch and raise the peak.

The west Lumbridge yew was guarded by a bear, and the bot died there. I’m recovering a knife, converting the retained yew logs, and using the proceeds to restore an axe before the final training window.

The retained yew bows sold at the general store, and I’ve upgraded to a steel axe. I’m using the safe cemetery yew for one last stocked batch; its higher XP per log gives the best chance to beat the current 527 XP/min peak.
The safe yew has supplied 24 logs, enough for a strong longbow burst. I’m timing the fletching pass to the fixed sampling clock so as many bows as possible land in one 15 second window.
The yew longbow burst raised the peak to 675 XP/min. I’m gathering one more full inventory and will start the next pass immediately after a sample boundary to reduce the split across windows.
The tree has a long respawn gap, so this final inventory is still filling. I’m watching the remaining benchmark time and will use whatever batch is ready before the clock ends.

The second stocked pass reached Fletching 85 and a 900 XP/min peak. There is still enough time for one more yew batch, so I’m using the remaining window to see whether tighter alignment can improve it.
There are 23 yew logs ready and one sampling window left. I’m fletching them now to make the final window count.

The 30-minute run is complete. **Peak Fletching rate: 900 real-game XP/min**, measured over a 15-second window. The character finished at **Fletching 86**.

The best result came from stocking yew logs and fletching yew longbows in one burst. The training script is saved at [train_fletching.ts](/app/bots/agent/train_fletching.ts).
I’ll start with the required single tutorial action, then establish a Thieving baseline and compare faster methods using the 15-second score checks.
The first pickpocket worked and gave 200 raw XP. I’m measuring a short repeated run now, then I’ll move to higher XP targets as levels unlock.
The Lumbridge loop reached Thieving 27 quickly, but the walk toward Al Kharid is waiting at the toll gate. I found the gate dialogue sequence and will use it to test warriors next.

Warriors give 400 raw XP per success and raised Thieving to 36, but stun damage is limiting the run. I bought kebabs for sustain and am moving toward Ardougne, where stalls and higher level pickpocket targets are clustered.

The safe baker’s stall is reliable: 8,400 raw XP in 30 seconds and no damage, with a current peak of 88 real-game XP/min. I’m testing guards and the higher level stalls now; both may raise the peak substantially.
Knights raised Thieving from 56 to 71 in 30 seconds; the peak is now 1,012 real-game XP/min. Paladins are unlocked, so I’m comparing their success rate and XP per success before moving to heroes.

Heroes give about 6,833 raw XP per success, but their catches are frequent and the 15-second test used most of the food. I’m restocking from the nearby baker, then I’ll compare longer knight, paladin, and hero windows at higher Thieving levels.

The west baker opens a shop and can supply a full inventory of food quickly. Heroes have raised the peak to 1,503 XP/min at level 93. I’m putting the food restock and hero loop into a background script so training continues while I monitor the score.

The automated loop is working and has reached Thieving 96. The hero sometimes wanders behind doors, which lowers some windows; the script returns to the reachable west side and restocks before resuming. I’m letting it continue toward 99, then I’ll use the remaining time to target the best 15-second window.

Thieving is now 99. The peak remains 1,503 XP/min; the limiting factor is how many hero successes land in one fixed 15-second window. I’m keeping the hero loop active and watching for a stronger window while food is restocked.

The background loop reached 99 but then died twice while trying to restock, so I stopped it. The score is preserved. I’m returning to Ardougne with a safer short run and will use the last few minutes for focused, food supplied hero attempts.

Repeated crossings of White Wolf Mountain are now the obstacle: the character has died to wolves before reaching Ardougne without food. I’m testing a southern waypoint once; if it still routes through the wolves, I’ll keep training locally through the end of the benchmark.
I made it back to Ardougne with 17 kebabs and full Thieving level. I’m using the final windows on the reachable west hero; the best recorded rate is still 1,503 XP/min.
I’ll start with the single tutorial action you specified, then get a Prayer XP baseline and test faster training methods.
Tutorial is complete. The nearby rat hasn’t produced Prayer XP, so I’m moving to chickens for a quick bones baseline while checking higher XP options.
Burying one chicken bone gave 112 raw Prayer XP, so the baseline works. I’m pursuing The Restless Ghost’s Prayer reward next, then I’ll compare it with faster repeatable bone training.
The quest is underway: I have the Ghostspeak amulet and the ghost has identified the skull’s location. I’m retrieving it from the Wizard Tower now.
The Restless Ghost is complete and Prayer reached level 47. Its reward landed as 28,125 raw XP in one event; I’m waiting for the next fixed sample, then I’ll target a higher single window.
The quest reward produced a measured peak of **563 real game XP/min**. Priest in Peril offers a larger Prayer reward, and its opening steps are available on this character, so I’ve started it.

The level 30 monk killed the character during the key fight. The quest progress remains, and the sword and Ghostspeak amulet were kept. I’m building the rune essence access needed for the quest’s final step, then I’ll return with melee protection for that fight.
Rune Mysteries is at its final delivery: Aubury’s notes are in hand. Finishing it will let me mine the 50 essence needed for Priest in Peril.
Rune Mysteries is complete, and the first 28 rune essence are mined. I’m banking them, collecting the remaining 22, then returning to Drezel’s quest.
The second essence run is in progress. The mining call has run longer than expected, so I’m checking whether it is still gaining essence before continuing the quest route.
I’ll start with the single tutorial action, then get a Fishing baseline and adjust the method based on the XP rate.
The character has a small net and is in Lumbridge. The local fishing guide points to Draynor for level 1 spots, so I’m heading there for the first catch.
The first net run caught five shrimp and reached Fishing 11. I’m clearing inventory space, then I’ll push to level 20 and test fly fishing, which has better XP per catch.
Fishing 35 is unlocked. I bought a fly rod, harpoon, lobster pot, and a small feather supply. I’m measuring a fly fishing burst before testing the no bait methods.
Fly fishing produced 21,750 raw XP in 25 seconds and raised Fishing from 35 to 50; the current peak sample is 250 real XP/min. I’m at Karamja now testing harpoon catches against that result.
At Karamja, a three second click interval gave 27,000 raw XP in 30 seconds, and Fishing is now 68. I’m automating lobster catches until level 76 so I can test shark fishing.
The sustained lobster run is working; Fishing has reached 72. The next test is a higher level spot once level 76 unlocks sharks.
Fishing is 76, and the Karamja lobsters paid for the return trip. I’m heading to the Catherby coast to test shark spots and compare their catch rate with lobsters.

At Fishing 83, a 4 second lobster click interval filled 22 slots in about 35 seconds. The best aligned sample has risen to **450 real XP/min**. I’m keeping that method running through level 99, then I’ll compare another interval at the higher level.
The sustained run has reached Fishing 86, and the peak is now **495 real XP/min**. The bot is still cycling Catherby lobster spots and clearing its inventory as it fills.
Fishing is 89 with nine minutes remaining. I’m switching to a shark comparison at this level; shark catches award more XP each, so the higher catch chance may now beat lobsters.

The level 90 lobster test with a 6 second click interval filled 22 slots in 24 seconds. The benchmark peak is now **585 real XP/min**, higher than the shark run. I’m using this cadence for the remaining time and watching for a better aligned window.

The 8 second test raised the aligned-window peak to **720 real XP/min**. Its average catch rate was lower, but the score rewards the best 15 second window, so I’m running that cadence through the remaining benchmark time.
The 8 second run has reached Fishing 95. The peak remains **720 real XP/min**, with another recent window at 675. The script is continuing until the benchmark ends.
Fishing is 97 with 75 seconds left in the benchmark. I’ve restarted the lobster loop for the final minute so the character keeps training through the last samples.

Fishing reached **level 99**. The benchmark score was **720 real-game XP/min**, from a 15-second window with 36,000 raw XP.

I tested net, fly rod, harpoon, big net, shark, and lobster fishing. The best scoring run used Catherby lobster spots with an 8-second click interval.
I’ll start with the requested single tutorial action, then get a Cooking XP baseline and adjust based on the measured 15-second peak.
The character starts at Cooking 1 with no raw food. I found a usable Lumbridge range and a documented level 1 fishing spot; I’m testing the shortest route to the first cooked item now.
The first shrimp cooked successfully: Cooking reached level 8 and the measured peak is 15 XP/min. I’m looking for a bulk raw-food source so a full inventory can be cooked inside one sampling window.
A 14-fish burst raised the peak to 135 XP/min and Cooking to 31. I’m switching to higher XP fish; the nearby shop sells the rod and feathers needed for trout and salmon.

Cooking is now 48 and Fishing 46. A permanent fireplace worked for the trout and salmon batch; the temporary campfire expired before it could be used reliably. I’m testing harpoon fishing next, since swordfish give substantially more Cooking XP per successful cook.
Harpooning works: Fishing reached 57 and the inventory has tuna and swordfish. I’m filling the remaining slots, then I’ll cook the batch at a permanent source and compare the measured peak.

The 25-fish range batch raised Cooking from 48 to 64 in about 11 seconds. The tracker’s latest reading still shows a window from before that batch; I’m waiting for the next fixed sample before judging the result.
The previous batch produced a measured peak of 1,040 XP/min. I’m now keeping swordfish and clearing tuna while fishing, so the next cooking burst uses more of the inventory’s highest XP fish.
Fishing has reached 72, with 15 swordfish held. I’m finishing the full swordfish inventory, then returning to the Port Sarim range for a single timed burst.

The swordfish batch raised the measured peak to 1,120 XP/min and Cooking to 73. I’m preparing one more full batch and will start cooking just after a sample boundary so the fixed 15-second window captures as much of it as possible.

The second swordfish run is underway. Fishing is already 76, which unlocks sharks; the immediate aim is a better aligned swordfish burst, then I’ll use the remaining time for higher XP fish if Cooking reaches the required level.
The aligned batch lifted the peak to 1,470 XP/min. Cooking is 79 and Fishing is 83, so I’m finishing the remaining swordfish and moving to Catherby to test sharks for a higher peak.

Cooking 80 is unlocked, and the Catherby shark spot is active. There are five minutes left; I’m gathering as many sharks as possible and will reserve the final window for cooking them at the nearby range.
The shark fishing loop is still running. Once it ends, I’ll cook the catch in one burst and check the tracker’s next complete 15-second sample.
I have 26 raw sharks at a reachable Catherby range, with 2 minutes 15 seconds left. I’m cooking the full inventory now, then I’ll use any remaining time to improve the peak.
I’ll skip the tutorial with a single action, then check the character’s state and start a short Crafting test. Once XP is flowing, I’ll compare methods using the 15-second score windows.
The character has 3 coins now. I’m using them to get shears and test wool spinning for the first Crafting XP, then I’ll move to a faster method if the materials allow it.

Spinning one wool gave 62 raw Crafting XP, so the method works. The score has not registered a full 15-second window yet. I’m clearing inventory space so I can gather and spin a full batch, which should give a more useful rate measurement.

The first wool batch is coming in slowly because some sheep evade shearing and a few targets become unreachable. I’m switching to nearby targets with shorter checks, then I’ll spin the wool in one run and compare the sampled rate.
The full wool batch reached 1,250 raw Crafting XP and a measured peak of 23 real-game XP/min. I’m turning in the Sheep Shearer quest now, then I’ll use the remaining time to test higher XP recipes.

Sheep Shearer completed and raised the peak to 75 real-game XP/min. The quest list shows larger Crafting rewards, so I’m heading to the short Murder Mystery quest next; its 1,406 XP reward would give a much stronger single sample.

Murder Mystery is underway: I have the crime scene items and flypaper for fingerprints. I need an ordinary pot for flour, so I’m getting one from the nearby Catherby shop and speaking with the poison salesman on the way back.

Murder Mystery is complete. Its reward raised the measured peak to 703 real-game XP/min, with Crafting now at level 52. I have about 14 minutes left and am checking whether Elemental Workshop’s larger reward is reachable from here.
I’m at the Observatory and will test its quest route next. The current measured peak is 703 real-game Crafting XP/min; I’m using the remaining time to try for a larger one-window reward.
I’ll start with the single tutorial action you specified, then get a working Firemaking baseline and use the rate checker to guide faster runs.
The first log burned successfully for 1,000 raw Firemaking XP. I’m checking the API and local game notes now so the next run can gather and burn logs in a repeatable loop.

The simple chop and burn loop reached a 180 XP/min peak. I’ve reached the Woodcutting level for willows, so I’m moving to a willow cluster and will test whether its higher XP per log improves a full sampling window.

Willow logs give 2,250 raw XP each, and a prepared stack burns quickly on an open east to west line. I’m clearing inventory space and stocking logs first; that should concentrate more burns inside one 15 second scoring window.
The Seers route crossed White Wolf Mountain and killed the character. I’m checking the respawn and will use a safer route for higher tier logs; the current willow batch may still be recoverable.

A 12 log willow burst succeeded with no failed lights, and Firemaking is now high enough for yew logs. I’m testing yew chopping and burning next; its larger XP per log may beat the willow burst even if gathering is slower.
Yew burns for 5,062 raw XP each. I found two yew trees beside Edgeville bank and am filling the inventory from both before a timed burn run.

The yew burst has raised the peak to 1,114 XP/min. A fire sometimes leaves the character on a blocked tile, so I’m adjusting the burn route and checking access to magic trees, which unlock at the current Woodcutting and Firemaking levels.
I found a cleaner row north of Edgeville where six yew logs burned without interruption. I’m filling another inventory to test a longer burst on that row.
Yew gathering is slower than willow gathering, but the prepared burns are what set the score. The next inventory is nearly full, and I’ll burn it in one pass to measure the cleaner route.

The full yew run landed 26 burns in a single scoring window: the peak is now **2,633 XP/min**. I’m using the remaining time to see whether I can reach magic trees safely and beat that with their higher XP per log.

I crossed the mountain via its southern path and reached Catherby with 3 HP, then recovered the axe and tinderbox from the bank. I’m heading to the magic trees now; this avoids repeating the risky crossing.
Magic logs work: one burn gave 7,595 raw XP. I’m stocking a full inventory from the Sorcerer’s Tower trees, then I’ll use an open burn lane for the next scoring attempt.
The magic tree harvest is still running. Its logs are much slower to collect than yew, so I’m keeping the run bounded and will use whatever it gathers for a measured burst.
The first harvest produced 14 magic logs and raised Woodcutting to 87. I’m filling the remaining slots now; once the batch is ready, the key will be lighting them continuously in a 15 second window.
The magic inventory is full. I found a mostly open field east of the tower and am running the prepared logs through adjacent rows now; that should show whether magic beats the 2,633 XP/min yew peak.
All 26 remaining magic logs burned successfully in 13 seconds. I’m gathering another batch so I can repeat the burst against the server’s fixed 15 second sampling clock.
The second magic batch is being harvested. I’ll check the recorded peak when this run finishes, then use the remaining time for a final burn attempt if the clock split the first one.
The magic harvest is taking longer than the burn itself, as expected. I’m keeping the batch moving and will use the same open row that supported the uninterrupted 26 log run.
The first magic burst scored **3,645 XP/min**; 24 burns landed in one fixed window. I’m filling the last inventory slots for one final chance to fit all 27 into a window.

The second magic burst again put 24 logs inside one scoring window, holding the peak at **3,645 XP/min**. There is one log left from a blocked tile; I’m burning it and using the remaining time for another short magic harvest.
The final short harvest and burn run is in progress. I’ll check the rate tracker once it finishes and report the recorded peak.
Completed the 30-minute Firemaking run. The recorded peak was **3,645 real-game XP/min**, with 24 magic logs burned in one 15-second sampling window. Firemaking finished at level 96.

I’ll skip the tutorial with the first bot action, then check the character’s gear and nearby targets to get an Attack XP baseline. I’ll compare the measured 15-second windows as I adjust the training loop.
The first 30-second combat run gained 6,800 raw Attack XP and reached level 30. I’m checking the benchmark’s aligned-window peak, then I’ll try stronger targets and better equipment.

Strength is now level 30, but the goblin run spent time chasing targets and sometimes left combat marked active after a kill. I’m moving to enemies with more HP and will select a fresh target when the current one disappears.
The walk toward Al Kharid is still running, so I’m checking whether a gate or route issue is delaying it. Once there, I’ll make a short combat trial before committing to that location.
Al Kharid warriors raised the peak to 160 real-game XP/min. Health fell to 10, so I’m collecting nearby coins and stocking food before another run.
I’ve bought nine kebabs. I’m building enough coins from nearby pickpockets for a steel scimitar, then I’ll retest Attack XP on the warriors with the stronger weapon.
I’ve reached 1,100 coins, enough for the listed mithril scimitar price. I’m buying it now, then I’ll use the remaining coins and warrior drops to keep food stocked during Attack training.
The mithril scimitar and Strength 55 raised the peak to 308 XP/min. The last run used all food and left 6 HP, so I’m retreating to restock before testing a higher Strength level.
The latest warrior run reached 368 XP/min with Strength 68. I’ll raise Strength further, then make another Attack run to see whether the extra damage improves the peak.
The new peak is 418 XP/min at Attack 77 and Strength 74. I’ll use the remaining time for another Strength increase, then make a final Attack push with food ready.
The last Attack run stalled behind palace doors: it found only unreachable warriors and barely gained XP. I’m moving to the courtyard with an exact destination, then rerunning the combat loop.

Attack is now level 82. The last run gained XP steadily, but its best aligned window did not beat 418 XP/min. I’ve corrected the target selection issue and will use the final few minutes for another sustained Attack run.
The sustained run brought Attack to level 87; the peak remains 418 XP/min. About a minute remains, so I’m using it for one last Attack burst and will check the final aligned-window score.

Training is complete. **Peak Attack rate: 420 real-game XP/min**, from 21,000 raw XP in the best 15-second window.

Attack rose from level 10 to **88**. The best run used a mithril scimitar against Al Kharid warriors after raising Strength to level 82.
I’ll start with the required single action, then check the character’s gear and nearby targets and get a Ranged XP baseline.
The bow and arrows are equipped, and the first attack is working. The API calls this action `bot.attack`; I’m switching to Rapid and checking where to get enough arrows for sustained training.

The bank is empty, so I’m raising a small amount of gold from starter items and pickpocketing. That should fund arrows from Lowe’s shop nearby; then I can spend the remaining time testing targets and weapons.
The cow test has raised the peak from 18 to 32 real-game XP/min so far. I’m letting this short run finish, then I’ll check ammo recovery and move to a target that can stay alive through more shots.

The direct route to Rimmington stops at a map barrier. I found a second route through Falador; I’m using a westward waypoint to reach the moss giants, whose 60 HP should keep attacks flowing within a sample window.

The hobgoblin pack killed the character, and the arrows were lost on death. I’ve respawned with the bow. I’m rebuilding coins through Thieving, then I’ll buy stronger ammo and use a safer single target for the next rate test.

The faster target switching helped: the peak is now 136 XP/min. The earlier loop was waiting through the post-kill combat cooldown, so I’m keeping this version and checking how much ammo it uses before choosing the next upgrade.

The cow loop reached Ranged 61 and a 168 XP/min peak, with seven arrows left. I’m testing the nearby farmer as a source of gold for another ammo run; it is closer than the guards and should let me keep training without another dangerous fight.

Steel arrows did not improve the cow peak; most of their extra damage is wasted against 8 HP cows. I’m switching back to bronze and testing direct attack commands, which may avoid the walking delay in the high-level attack helper.

Direct attack commands raised the peak to 224 XP/min and Ranged to 69. The cow field is now short on live targets, so I’m funding a larger arrow batch and testing guards, which have more HP per target.

The guard test averaged below the cow loop and used the steel arrows quickly. I’m collecting the nearby drops, then moving to Al Kharid warriors. They have more HP than cows and access to cheap food for a longer bronze-arrow test.

The guard stayed in combat after the steel arrows ran out and killed the character before I moved away; the bow survived, but the bronze stack was lost. I’m rebuilding ammo from the current Thieving level, then I’ll finish on cows, where the best score came from.

The fresh bronze stack pushed the peak to 258 XP/min. I found a possible safe ranged target at the Wizard’s Tower with much more HP; after this cow run, I’ll test whether its hit rate beats the cow field.
I’ll start with the required one-action tutorial call, then check the character and get a Smithing XP baseline before trying faster methods.
The character starts at level 1 Smithing with no ores or bars. I found a documented copper and tin mine and a furnace route, so I’m collecting a small batch to establish the first XP sample.
The first bronze bar gave Smithing XP, so the baseline is live. I’m smelting the rest of this batch, then I’ll compare forging XP and look for a faster supply loop.

Forging is faster than smelting: the first 12 bronze bars became four items for 3,750 raw forging XP. I’m moving to iron now; its higher XP per bar should produce a better 15-second peak if I build up enough bars first.

Iron smelting produced 9 bars from 26 ores, and forging those brought Smithing to level 38. I’m doing one more iron batch to unlock gold smelting, then I’ll test a full inventory of gold ore for the peak window.

Gold ore is available at Al Kharid, but nearby scorpions are interrupting mining and have cut the character to 10 HP. I’m moving to safety, smelting the ore already collected, and checking a safer gold source before committing to a longer run.

The Al Kharid gold test confirmed 562 raw Smithing XP per successful smelt. I’ve banked the spare items and am checking the Barbarian Village gold rocks, where the mining trip should be safer if they are reachable.
